industry.why: Underweight, carried; neither way back to Neutral is met: the US ten-year is 4.83% (Goldman Sachs, 20 to 26-Nov) against the 4.5% trigger, and industry relative strength is F (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; D prior). The Telecoms Industry Memo (26-Nov) finds no industry tailwind, neutral at three and six months; the week to 25-Nov was the first since October in which Telecoms moved with the other defensives (+2.0 points against the index), one week against a grade of F. The 27-Nov-26 regime (yields falling as a safety bid, not on easing) does not yet pay leveraged yield defensives; this is among the first rows to lift if the ten-year goes under 4.5% on an easing read. No Pool name, no live holding. Counter-case: the trigger is 33 basis points away, closer than at any read since the row was set. To C on industry relative strength above 30 by end-January with stable churn and pricing, or the ten-year under 4.5%.

sector.why: Underweight, carried with the industry's letter (the 33 mobile network operators are the industry): the US ten-year is 4.83% against the 4.5% trigger, relative strength F (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; D prior), the Telecoms Industry Memo (26-Nov) finds no tailwind, and the Vodafone and Telefonica results did not reach the pack. No Pool name, no live holding. Counter-case: the base rate (55% of past cases back above the 200-day within 26 weeks) is Neutral and the trigger is 33 basis points away. Back to C on industry relative strength above 30 by end-January with stable churn and pricing, or the ten-year under 4.5%; to F on a lower low or churn attributed to satellites or switching tools.

geography.why: Double Underweight, carried, now on fresh evidence rather than the stale spread: France's forward-looking PMI fell to 46.2 to 46.8, near its record low, 'a deepening downturn' (S&P Global via Pivotus, 23-Nov; Goldman Economics, 24-Nov), Pivotus calls it 'a disaster', Macron is considering a constitutional 'golden rule' if markets stay unstable in January with Le Pen leading the polls (Pivotus, 23-Nov), and Stehn (Goldman, 22-Nov) expects France to stagnate until its elections. The premium in basis points was unread for a fourth week, so last week's staleness rule (to D if unread again) is overtaken by the political and activity evidence, said plainly. 15 Pool stocks are French-listed, most of them global businesses. Counter-case: a top letter on a country whose listed companies earn mostly abroad, and the mid-2027 election is far away. To D when the premium is read under 120 basis points for a month with the PMI off its low; to C under 100.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
